name: input.mouse.scroll
description: Send mouse-wheel notches at virtual-screen coordinates. Each notch translates to `system.info.capabilities.input_settings.wheel_scroll_lines` lines per OS convention.

x.description: X in virtual-screen coordinates. Off-screen requests are clamped.

delta.description: Wheel notches. Positive = scroll up (away from user); negative = scroll down. Each notch is `WHEEL_DELTA` (120) Win32 units.

horizontal.description: Horizontal wheel (tilt or shift+wheel) instead of vertical. Default false. Agents that lack horizontal-wheel support fall back to ignoring the flag.

x.description: Clamped X the wheel event was synthesised at.

x-implementations.name: send_input
x-implementations.description: Win32 `SendInput` with INPUT_MOUSE + `MOUSEEVENTF_WHEEL` (vertical) or `MOUSEEVENTF_HWHEEL` (horizontal). Delta is multiplied by `WHEEL_DELTA` (120) to produce the dwData value.

x-implementations.name: mouse_event
x-implementations.description: Win32 `mouse_event` with `MOUSEEVENTF_WHEEL` legacy fallback for NT 4 / 9x. No horizontal wheel support pre-NT-6 (Vista).

windows-modern.description: SendInput with MOUSEEVENTF_WHEEL / MOUSEEVENTF_HWHEEL. The OS lines-per-notch setting is exposed via `system.info.capabilities.input_settings.wheel_scroll_lines` (typically 3, but user-configurable via Mouse Properties). UIPI applies same as input.mouse.click.

windows-classic.description: SendInput on NT 5+; mouse_event on NT 4 / 9x. Vertical wheel via MOUSEEVENTF_WHEEL is widely supported. Horizontal wheel (MOUSEEVENTF_HWHEEL) is Vista+ — pre-Vista classic agents silently ignore `horizontal: true`.
